articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Intelligent Cardiac Implants' (Digest No.022)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelligent Cardiac Implants
IEE Colloquium on Intelligent Cardiac Implants
abstract: The author presents a general assessment of the range of sensor used in rate-adaptive pacing: activity sensors, Q-T interval, respiratory sensors, paced depolarisation integral, accelerometer based sensors, dual sensors. Some aspects of clinical practice and mimicking of sinus rhythm are also addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recording pacemakers memory size-what should be recorded
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelligent Cardiac Implants
abstract: A modified form of electrogram recording element was used in conjunction with an implanted anti-tachycardiac pacemaker employing a telemetry link. This permitted long term monitoring of the intra-cardiac electrogram signal during a series of mode switching operations carried out by the implanted device. The basic instrument included a 16 second circular buffer continuously recording the electrogram and pressure waveforms by overwriting the oldest data. On detection of an arrhythmia a portion of each waveform just before and after the event would be 'frozen' for subsequent studies. In the prototype system an 8192 (8 k) byte buffer was used. The electrogram was sampled at 400 samples per second and the pressure signal at 100 samples per second, allowing just over 16 seconds of each event to be stored. A 128 k byte static RAM module was used to implement the circular buffer and for storing recording wave forms. A total of 16 events could be retained in the memory at any time. A further 2 k bytes of static RAM was available for use by the programme and for the storage of statistical data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelligent Cardiac Implants
abstract: A system consisting of implantable cardio-synchronous myostimulation (CSM) device, intramuscular leads and programmer is presented. The device is capable of delivering relatively high-energy pulse trains to the muscle. The frequency of pulses, energy delivered for each pulse (voltage amplitude and width), and total number of pulses (or duration of the burst) is configurable. Ventricular demand or asynchronous pacing is provided. The delay time from the sensed QRS-complex or pacing pulse is programmable. The device is capable of a range of heart beat to myostimulation burst ratios, form 1:1 to 10:1. It is usual for the muscle stimulation to occur during every second cardiac cycle. The burst duration and frequency and the heart beat to burst ratio may be independently configured over three heart rate ranges. Additionally, the interval between burst pulses may be incremented or decremented during burst delivery.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Safety-critical aspects of ICDs and pacemakers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelligent Cardiac Implants
abstract: Areas of interest concerning the safety and efficacy of implantable cardiovertors/defibrillators and pacemakers are discussed. These include: spike loss; oversensing; crosstalk; radiation effects; inappropriate shocks; device proarrhythmia.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signal processing for ICDs; recognition of normal and abnormal rhythms
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelligent Cardiac Implants
abstract: A problem that has emerged with the wider use of an implantable defibrillator is that the device may deliver an inappropriate discharge because it has failed to discriminate between ventricular and nonventricular arrhythmics at a heart rate that is deemed to be dangerous. Automatic rhythm diagnosis by implantable devices is not a simple problem. The development of an automatic method of tachycardia diagnosis and its potential success are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Types of sensor for rate responsive pacemakers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelligent Cardiac Implants
abstract: The author briefly outlines the various current sensor systems for cardiac pacemakers. Some details as to their relative strengths and weaknesses, and intelligent sensing possibilities, are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
